To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Gut-derived GIP activates Rap1 to impair hypothalamic lepti sensitivity during overnutrition.

the gut-derived incretein GIP, through the activation of the GIPR, increases the activity of the small G protein Rap1, and this activation impairs neural leptin sensitivity and contributes to obesity in mice.

the gut-derived incretein hormone GIP activates the small GTP-binding protein Rap1 in the hypothalamus to impair hypothalamic leptinsensitivity during nutrient excess, and that the inhibition of this GIP-Rap1 pathway by central administration of a neutralizing antibody for GIPR protects against obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how obesity affects the ability of leptin to regulate body weight and adipose tissue mass.
how the brain controls body weight and fat mass, and how this control is disrupted by overnutrition.
the mechanisms that underlie the development of neural leptin resistance in obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GIP is an incretin that is released by the gut in response to nutrient ingestion and that acts in the brain to promote obesity by impairing hypothalamic sensitivity of the leptin receptor.
GIPR/RAP1 signaling in the hypothalamus is a novel mechanism that links nutrient excess to the development of obesity and neural leptin resistance.
GIPR/RAP1 signaling in the CNS is a key pathway linking overnutrition and the control of hypothalamic leptinsensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GIPR/RAP1 pathway in the brain plays an important role in the control of hypothalamic sensitivity of leptin.
the GIP/GIPR/Rap signaling in the brain is required for the development of neural leptin resistance and obesity.
gut-derived GIP activates brain Rap1 to impair hypothalamic leptinsensitivity, thereby promoting obesity and diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut hormone GIP, which is released from the gut in response to nutrients, is a physiological signal that controls the central actions of leptin.
the gut hormone GIP can act in the brain to impair leptin signaling and promote weight gain during overnutrition.
the gut-derived incretins GIP and GLP-1 are not only involved in the control of glucose homeostasis, but they can also control energy balance.
